exchanges: Good evening! I've had a long day, but I wanted to talk through a few things about this weekend.
Good evening. Happy to help, what's happening this weekend?
We have our five-a-side final on Saturday. Our team is called the Rusty Boots, which tells you everything about our skill level.
That's a great name. Reaching a final is impressive whatever the name says.
Thanks. Our captain, Rafael, has been driving everyone to matches since he got his new Corolla, which is nice of him.
That's generous of him. A reliable lift makes a big difference for an amateur team.
Coach Dmitri wants us to play more defensively, but honestly we only win when we attack.
It's worth telling him that, ideally with a couple of examples from recent matches.
Maybe. Dmitri used to play semi-professionally in Latvia, so it's hard to argue with him.
That experience gives him credibility, but he still needs to fit the plan to the players he has.
True. Unrelated, but my sister moved to Leeds last month and I'm planning to visit her in November.
That's a nice reason for a trip. Has she settled in?
Mostly. She took a job at a university library there.
That sounds like a calm, pleasant place to work.
It is. Meanwhile my brother Vikram and his wife Meera have just moved to Bristol, so the whole family is scattering.
It does sound like everyone is spreading out. At least Leeds and Bristol are both easy to reach by train.
Meera is thrilled because she can finally get a dog. She's had her eye on a whippet for years.
Those are lovely dogs, very gentle at home and fast outdoors.
Ananya is jealous. Her landlord doesn't allow pets.
That's a shame. Maybe she can borrow her sister-in-law's dog when she visits.
Ha, maybe. Back to football, do you have any advice for calming nerves before a final?
A consistent warm-up routine helps, and so does focusing on your first few touches rather than the result.
I tend to overthink penalties. I missed one in the semi-final.
Pick your spot before you walk up and don't change it. Indecision is what usually causes the miss.
Good advice. Hiroko, my neighbour, said the same thing. She played hockey at a national level.
She'd know about pressure moments, then.
She's also the reason I took up bouldering, which has helped my leg strength a lot.
Bouldering is great for grip and balance too, which carries over to most sports.
I should correct something I said earlier. Rafael's car is actually a Civic, not a Corolla. I got them confused.
Thanks for clarifying. Either way, it's a sensible car for ferrying a team around.
Yes, and it fits five of us if we squeeze.
Cosy, but it works for a five-a-side team.
Exactly. Do you think I should get new boots before Saturday or stick with my old ones?
Stick with the old ones. New boots right before a final risk blisters.
That's what I thought. They're falling apart a little, but they're comfortable.
Comfort wins on match day. Replace them after the final.
Our goalkeeper, Kwame, is injured, so we might have to play someone out of position.
That's tough. What happened to him?
He sprained his wrist at work. He's a carpenter, so it happened with a nail gun, which sounds worse than it was.
Ouch. Wrists take a while to heal, so it's sensible for him to sit out.
We're thinking Rafael might go in goal, since he's the tallest.
Height helps, but reflexes and confidence matter just as much. Has he played there before?
Once, years ago. He let in seven goals.
Then maybe a short practice session before Saturday would help everyone's nerves.
Good idea. I'll suggest Thursday evening.
Thursday gives enough time to practise without tiring anyone out.
Dmitri also wants us to wear matching socks, which feels like a strange priority.
It's a small thing, but it can help a team feel organised.
He bought them himself, bright orange ones. He said they make us easier to spot when passing.
There's some sense in that. Bright kit can help with quick passes.
I'll admit they're growing on me. I'm going to try to get an early night before work tomorrow.
That sounds sensible. Rest well.

questions.message: Which city did my sister-in-law end up in?
What does our keeper do for a living again?
Rafael drives a Civic, doesn't he?
What colour did the coach go for?
What kind of dog does Hiroko have?
I've just set two alarms so I don't oversleep.
